status: All36 mathematics source duties have prepared task designs with scoped components; sourceFull is not observed pupil or whole-topic mastery.

processes.task: Offer a neutral tray of blocks and ribbons. Learner chooses an answerable quantity/fit/measurement question, identifies needed information and selects concrete tools or a drawing. Solve it, explain/show the reason, compare another approach or a supplied incorrect answer, connect the concrete result and representation, then reflect on whether the tool and strategy answered the question. Change the available shape/length or quantity and revise the model/prediction when the physical check disagrees. Use this same process across number, shape and measure activities rather than a vocabulary recital.
processes.positive: An own problem, justified strategy, reflection, real connection, communication, representation and deliberate tool choice all occur across the portfolio.
processes.transfer: Change from a quantity scene to a ribbon-fit or shape problem; a copied numerical question alone does not show this breadth.

quantities-and-numerals.task: Use real numeral contexts (quantity label, place in an ordered sequence and an arbitrary toy-box identifier), without pretending every number is a count. Read and actually write shuffled0–20 numerals and match relevant quantities. Count actual sets to20 with one object per spoken number and state the total. Add/remove one and compare the change; count forward in ones from7,14 and18 to20, and use a decreasing concrete set to explain backwards counting. Show0 as an empty set, not a missing answer. Do not require recitation to100 for these source duties. Use the existing0–20 quantity/ordering operations with the actual changed starting number.
quantities-and-numerals.positive: Numerals and quantities connect while arbitrary identifiers/ordered uses are distinguished. A memorised song or tracing every answer supplied by an adult is insufficient.
quantities-and-numerals.transfer: Rearrange objects or change the starting numeral; count/identify/write again. No all100-number claim from a0–20 task.

parts-comparison-estimation.task: Flash different arrangements containing1–5 counters; ask how many without one-by-one counting, with accessible viewing time rather than a fixed speed norm. Compose/decompose collections to10 using actual two-part partitions, recombine and show a different split. Match two sets to compare more/equal/fewer despite changed spacing. For actual collections9,13 and18, first estimate against a visible reference group of5, then count to check and discuss the comparison; do not show the exact count before the estimate. Compare supported pairs0/7,8/13,16/20 using quantities, ordering and a number track; explain a similarity/difference, such as20 being4more than16.
parts-comparison-estimation.positive: Instant small-group recognition, reversible parts, matching comparison and an estimate recorded before exact counting are distinct checks.
parts-comparison-estimation.transfer: Use a new collection/layout and changed number pair; do not replace small-set estimation with rounding a supplied calculation.
parts-comparison-estimation.wholeClaimBoundary: Use the independently assessed shared quantity-estimation operation. The older numbers-to120 claim and its estimation requirement remain unchanged; no full120-number or cross-topic mastery is inferred. Use a fresh unknown-total target for a new estimation trial; a known counted set’s correct unchanged total is cardinality, not a gap.

operations-and-equal-sharing.task: Share6counters between2plates and8between4plates, checking equal shares and the whole; allow dealing one at a time, grouping or a drawing. Solve concrete within10 add/take/part-whole stories, such as4blocks joined by3,8with2removed, and7split into5and2. Practise and retrieve within5 addition and related subtraction facts, then check the relation with materials; do not count every recalled fact as fluent retrieval. Change the context and unknown while preserving the intended relationship.
operations-and-equal-sharing.positive: Actual equal distribution, operation meaning, concrete problem solution and fact retrieval are separately observed.
operations-and-equal-sharing.transfer: Use a new within10 situation and a new equal-share arrangement; no advanced written division or remainder law is inferred.

canadian-money.task: Use accurate adult-prepared play coins/bills or supervised appropriate real money:5¢nickel,10¢dime,25¢quarter,$1loonie,$2toonie,$5and$10notes. Identify by more than one available feature and state/explore the value; distinguish money amount from the number or physical size of pieces. Compare a nickel/dime and different designs of the same denomination. Build simple equivalent amounts such as two5¢coins and one10¢coin, or two$5notes and one$10note; cents/dollars remain explicit, not an invented1coin=1dollar rule. No penny is described as currently minted/distributed, and no private family income/purchase is needed.
canadian-money.positive: Recognition and value relationships survive changed orientation/design rather than a silhouette or size ranking.
canadian-money.transfer: Use a changed accurate example or same-value combination within source scope. Broader existing whole local-currency inventory remains separately assessed.

repeating-patterns.task: Build and describe original ABB and AAB sequences with cubes or sounds. Mark the smallest repeat, explain why it determines continuation, translate the same core into a different material/sound representation, create another repeat, extend both left and right and replace a concealed missing element. Compare a visually different representation retaining the same core and a near miss with a changed core.
repeating-patterns.positive: Core structure, translation, bidirectional continuation and missing-element repair all occur.
repeating-patterns.transfer: Use a new core/material and a missing item inside rather than only appending the next item.

data-and-likelihood.task: Choose an answerable observational question about an actual prepared set of8buttons/counters (adult fixture:3red,2blue,3yellow). Learner sorts by one declared attribute, counts and records the observations before seeing the key, and constructs an aligned one-object-per-response concrete graph and a one-picture-per-object graph. Add a title, categories and actual source/date. Interpret the tied most categories and fewer blue objects, explain a supported conclusion and what the small prepared set does not say about every classroom. For likelihood use a physically checked opaque bag:3red+1yellow, then all red, then no red; describe likely/certain/impossible and distinguish possible from guaranteed. Where used, an equal red/yellow bag gives even chance rather than calling half the outcomes likely.
data-and-likelihood.positive: Actual collection/recording and both concrete/picture interpretation are demonstrated; a supplied dataset alone is only practice. Likelihood descriptions are justified from the actual bag.
data-and-likelihood.transfer: Change the set/question or bag contents and revise the display/conclusion/likelihood. No inference from8objects to a larger population.

shapes-space-and-measure.task: Handle varied real models/flat cut-outs, including circles, hexagons, rhombi and trapezoids, and cubes, spheres, prisms, cones and pyramids. Identify, sort and compare observable attributes, not orientation stereotypes. Build own3Dstructures and identify component solids and flat face shapes. Make a2Dpattern-block picture and a3Dblock structure with matching halves, explicitly checking both. Compose, separate and rearrange a flat composite (two right triangles into a rectangle, hexagon-block puzzle); name the components and show another arrangement. Describe location/movement and compare actual views of the same model from different positions, predicting a view before looking. Give ANDfollow a changed safe route. For measures choose the relevant attribute, directly compare two lengths, cover/overlay two areas, compare mass using a balance and capacity through controlled filling; then use a third string/shape/template/container/balance reference when direct comparison is unavailable and explain the go-between. Area is coverage, not boundary length; capacity is how much fits, not simply height.
shapes-space-and-measure.positive: Own construction and both2D/3Dmatching, reversible composition, view prediction, reciprocal routing and direct/indirect comparison of all four attributes are individually checked.
shapes-space-and-measure.transfer: Use rotated/nonstandard shapes, a changed route/view, or a pair that must be compared indirectly. No claim of professional drawing, formal angle inventory or unit-square formula mastery.
shapes-space-and-measure.wholeClaimBoundary: The changed-view source task reuses recognition of a solid in different orientations at conservative age-six scope. It does not require the separate older orthographic top/front/side drawing or reconstruction claim. Preserve full older claim checks separately; a position word alone does not show visualisation.
